predecessors.name: Kingdom of Denmark
predecessors.text: Denmark with Cnut's English conquests as Cliopatria draws them in 1015-1017 (146,440 km2)

predecessors.name: Kingdom of England
predecessors.text: the English kingdom Cnut held from 1016; Cliopatria's England row (69,148 km2 in 1015-1017) has no shape between 1018 and 1045

successors.name: Kingdom of Denmark
successors.text: Denmark under Harthacnut, who succeeded his father there in 1035 (N2: 'In Denmark, he was succeeded by Harthacnut, reigning as Cnut III.')

successors.name: Kingdom of England
successors.text: England under Harold Harefoot, regent 1035-1037 and king until his death in 1040 (N2)

successors.name: Old Kingdom of Norway
successors.text: Norway under Magnus, brought back from Gardariki to rule (N1: 1034; Sweyn and Ælfgifu fled in autumn 1035)

ledger.x: 1018: Cnut, already king of England, becomes king of Denmark and rules both.
1031: Malcolm II of Scotland submits to Cnut.
Autumn 1035: Norway slips away from Cnut's sons.
12 November 1035: Cnut's death ends the submission of the Scottish kings.
12 November 1035: Cnut dies and the North Sea Empire falls apart.

wars.name: Cnut against Olaf II and Anund Jacob (Battle of the Helgeå)
wars.outcome: Olaf II attacked Denmark; N1 has Cnut defeating him at the Helgeå while noting that Anglo-Saxon sources credit Anund Jacob with the victory; no frontier moved.

wars.name: Cnut's conquest of Norway
wars.outcome: Olaf Haraldsson expelled; Cnut acclaimed at Nidaros and Sweyn Knutsson set up as his ruler in Norway (N2 puts the arrangement after Stiklestad, 1030).

wars.name: Magnus's return to Norway
wars.outcome: Magnus, Olaf's son, is brought back from Gardariki; Sweyn Knutsson and Ælfgifu flee in autumn 1035 and Norway leaves the empire.

certainty.note: A union of three crowns; the English and Danish edges are old frontiers, the Norwegian and Scottish edges are the limit of Cnut's authority, none fixed by treaty.
